notes: Line-by-line check. NHS excerpts support: hypoglycaemia as the main risk with the listed warning signs (sweating, trembling, fast heartbeat, tingling lips, dizziness, hunger, pale skin), injection-site itching/redness/bleeding/bruising and lipohypertrophy delaying absorption with site rotation, allergic reactions. The only numeric treatment figure (15-20 g fast sugar) predates the patch; no insulin dose figure was added and regimen descriptions (basal-bolus, once/twice daily basal) are NHS regimen descriptions, not instructions. Five-family classification, detemir twice daily vs glargine/degludec once, inhaled insulin lung caution, units written in full and brand non-interchangeability are standard NHS/MedlinePlus/NPSA content. Pre-patch items on weight gain, DKA if insulin omitted and hypokalaemia with IV infusion were dropped by the writers (loss of a safety point, noted for the editor; not within this verdict's remit). No protected field changed.
